thread.title: Stock futures point to gains following Tuesday's pummeling

author: Ken Martin
title: Stock futures point to gains following Tuesday's pummeling
text:
Dow gets pop from Chevron, Exxon Mobil By Suzanne O'Halloran Published November 21, 2018 Markets Fed's Kaplan on interest rates: We'd be wise to be very patient from here Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas President Robert Kaplan on the Federal Reserve's strategy for raising interest rates.
Energy shares, including Dow members Chevron and Exxon Mobil, helped lift U.S. stocks on Wednesday as global oil prices stabilized after the worst drop for U.S. crude in three years.
Ticker Security Last Change %Chg CVX CHEVRON CORP. 118.91 +2.81 +2.42% XOM EXXON MOBIL CORPORATION 78.28 +1.31 +1.71% USO UNITED STATES OIL FUND L.P. 11.70 +0.43 +3.82% Investors also took a fresh shine to large cap tech names, many of which have taken a beating over the past several weeks. The so-called FANG stocks, Facebook, Apple, Amazon, Netflix and Google, got a pop on Wednesday after shedding a combined $1 trillion plus in value from their record highs. Apple, which is sitting in a bear market, down 20 percent from its October high also climbed.

Defensive sectors, such as utlities and consumer staples, were lower.

The drop in global crude prices remain a big focus for world investors, as well as President Trump. On Tuesday, in a statement he indicated the U.S. will continue its working relationship with Saudi Arabia and later told reporters oil prices were in "great shape." He followed up with a fresh tweet on Wednesday thanking the Saudis and touting "oil prices are getting lower."
In deal news, Humana and Walgreens are reportedly in talks, according to The Wall Street Journal. This comes as Aetna and CVS prepare to close their $69 billion deal after the Thanksgiving holiday.

Gap —the owner of Old Navy, Banana Republic, and Athleta—says its namesake store Gap is dragging down its overall sales and is looking into closing hundreds of the brand’s locations “with urgency.”

There are mounting concerns about the pace of global growth which spurred fresh declines in stocks around the world, most notably wiping out yearly advances for the S&P 500, Dow Jones Industrial Average, while the Nasdaq Composite hung on to fractional gains.
U.S. stocks sold off across the board on Tuesday with the Dow Jones Industrial Average falling over 600 points, before trimming those declines. Losses accelerated in the final hour of trading as all major S&P 500 sectors tumbled led by energy, industrials, financials and tech. The volatility, in what is a short trading week due to Thanksgiving, erased yearly gains for the Dow, S&P 500 and essentially the Nasdaq Composite.
